Category.reason: Confirmed. The model inputs are qEEG/ERP measures from the eVox system and volumetric MRI from Neuroreader. The eVox recording is 19-channel EEG: eyes-open and eyes-closed resting state plus a Go/No-Go ERP task, and its final predictors are P300b amplitude, Reaction Time and Commission Errors. The final MRI predictor is left temporal lobe volume. These are C2 and C1; the title, abstract and keywords ('electroencephalography, magnetic resonance imaging') name them as the study's data. Chart-review clinical data (MMSE, demographics) supply the diagnostic labels and act as covariates. The registry's C5 omits the primary domain, C2 (and also C1), which the brief defines as an error. Reaction Time and Commission Errors are task-performance measures recorded during the ERP test, so a secondary C5 (or C4) could be added. Any correct code must contain C2;C1.
Category.quote: We investigated diagnostic categorization using an FDA-cleared quantitative electroencephalographic/event-related potential (qEEG/ERP)-based cognitive testing system (eVox® by Evoke Neuroscience) combined with an automated volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (vMRI) tool (Neuroreader® by Brainreader).
Category.supporting_quote: P300b amplitude, Reaction Time, and Commission Errors were found to significantly differentiate participants with SCD, MCI, and dementia (AUC = 0.79).
